title: An operation form coerces only a compatible material class
summary: A narrow selectional model says one operation form accepts a predeclared argument class; an incompatible class requires a distinct coercion form or is disallowed.

design.mechanism: typed argument selection with explicit coercion
design.unit: same operation in records whose candidate argument classes differ
design.contrast: type-compatible operation versus free lexical operation
design.prediction: Holding operation and context fixed, replacing the argument with an incompatible class should change the form to the coercion variant or remove the operation; compatible substitutions preserve the form.
design.countermodel: A context-conditioned lexical convention or editorial repetition could generate the same surface pattern without the proposed operation rule.
design.falsifier: The same form accepts incompatible classes without a coercion marker, or compatible classes require different forms for no other scoped change.
design.principal_risk: Independent argument types and coercion meanings are unavailable. Near IDEA000064 argument agreement, but this predicts acceptability/coercion, not modifier agreement.
